newsitem.title: BELGIUM: E.Europe seen having small sugar surplus in 2005.
newsitem.headline: E.Europe seen having small sugar surplus in 2005.

text.p: A recent increase in beet sugar yield and area is expected to lead to a small sugar surplus in 2005 in 10 East European countries seeking to join the EU, European Commission projections showed.
A 454,000 tonne sugar deficit in 1994 is expected to give way to a surplus of 4,000 tonnes in 2005.
The EU's sugar surplus is seen growing from 2.8 million tonnes to 3.5 million over the same period.

East European beet sugar output is expected to grow to 3.91 million tonnes in 2005, from 2.7 million in 1994 while domestic use is seen climbing to 3.90 million, from 3.1 million over the same period.

But difficulties in the processing industry meant it was doubtful whether the projected surplus would be sustained, the Commission's agriculture department said in an overview of long-term market trends.
